skill.name: plan-prospecting
skill.description: Research named employers and build sourced retirement-plan prospecting briefs using PlanProvider.Pro MCP data and Form 5500-derived signals.
skill.summary: Create evidence-based retirement-plan prospect lists from named employer targets.
skill.author: oil-can-man

security_audit.summary: The skill is a prompt-only research workflow with no executable code. Both hardcoded URLs are expected PlanProvider.Pro service references, and no malicious behavior or prompt injection was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL is the documented PlanProvider.Pro MCP endpoint that users intentionally configure for this skill. It contains no embedded credentials or evidence of covert data transfer.
This placeholder URL documents an expected GET request to the named PlanProvider.Pro service for source verification. It contains no secret, executable payload, or unrelated destination.

content.value_statement: Retirement-plan prospecting often lacks verified provider and plan context. This skill builds sourced briefs from named employers using PlanProvider.Pro and Form 5500-derived data.
actual_capabilities: Looks up retirement-plan records for user-supplied sponsor names.
Checks candidate matches using sponsor, plan, EIN, participant, asset, and filing details.
Identifies listed auditors, advisors, administrators, insurers, and ERISA attorneys.
Retrieves provider profiles by known provider slug.
Ranks named prospects using explicit filing-derived signals and labeled inferences.
Produces sourced markdown tables or concise ranked lists.
limitations: Requires a PlanProvider.Pro MCP connection and completed OAuth authorization.
Does not provide an unrestricted bulk export of employers.
Form 5500 data can lag, change through amendments, or describe an earlier filing period.
Does not replace a CRM, current contact database, or legal and fiduciary advice.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Audit Prospects
use_cases.description: Compare named employer plans and identify evidence-backed audit service opportunities.

use_cases.title: Prepare Advisor Outreach
use_cases.description: Research current plan providers and filing signals before contacting target sponsors.

use_cases.title: Validate Provider Relationships
use_cases.description: Confirm listed providers and source dates for a focused employer account list.

prompt_templates.title: Research One Employer
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [employer] with PlanProvider.Pro. Confirm the plan match and report the filing year, participants, assets, current providers, and canonical source URL.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a sourced profile for one target account.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Named Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these employers: [list]. Return confirmed plan matches in a table with filing dates, plan size, current providers, and source URLs.
prompt_templates.scenario: A sales professional needs a consistent comparison across a short target list.

prompt_templates.title: Find Service Opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [employer list] for [service]. Rank confirmed plans using filing-derived signals. Separate verified facts from inferences and explain every ranking.
prompt_templates.scenario: A specialist wants evidence-based prioritization for a defined service.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Advanced Territory Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [employer list] within [geography] for [service]. Resolve alternate sponsor names, verify provider details, and fetch canonical pages when MCP fields are incomplete.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced researcher needs deeper validation across a focused territory.

output_examples.input: Research three named Colorado employers for potential 401(k) audit outreach.
output: Confirmed targets appear in a table with plan name, filing year, participants, assets, auditor, outreach signal, and source URL.
Each outreach signal is labeled as a verified fact or an inference.
Unmatched employers appear separately with the attempted sponsor names.

output_examples.input: Compare listed advisors and recordkeepers for five target sponsors.
output: The ranked list identifies each confirmed sponsor, plan, advisor, recordkeeper, filing date, and canonical source.
Potential service gaps include a concise rationale based only on returned filing data.
The brief notes that listed relationships may not represent current arrangements.

best_practices: Provide a narrow list of named employers and define the service being sold.
Verify matches with sponsor, plan, EIN, plan number, filing year, participants, and assets.
Keep verified facts separate from inferences and include a canonical source for every result.
anti_patterns: Do not claim complete market coverage because the MCP does not offer unrestricted bulk exports.
Do not invent provider relationships, contacts, intent signals, plan sizes, fees, or credentials.
Do not present filing-period data or inferred opportunities as current verified facts.

faq.question: What information do I need to provide?
faq.answer: Provide named employers, target geography, desired plan type, approximate size, and the service you offer.

faq.question: Can this skill search every employer in a market?
faq.answer: No. It researches named candidates and does not provide an unrestricted bulk company export.

faq.question: Does the skill require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. Connect the PlanProvider.Pro MCP and complete its OAuth flow. Account tier controls available rows and fields.

faq.question: How does the skill verify a plan match?
faq.answer: It compares sponsor, plan name, EIN, plan number, participants, assets, filing year, and the canonical source.

faq.question: Are provider relationships always current?
faq.answer: No. Form 5500 data can lag, be amended, or describe a prior filing period.

faq.question: What output does the skill produce?
faq.answer: It returns a concise markdown table or ranked list with confirmed plan details, provider context, signals, inferences, and source URLs.
